findings.symbol: tests/test_contract.py::_k16_settled_elsewhere -- `body = br.body if isinstance(br, ast.IfExp) else br.body`
findings.detail: A TERNARY WHOSE TWO ARMS ARE THE SAME EXPRESSION, in a function whose whole point is an asymmetry the reader is being asked to trust. The line reads as though an IfExp's body were fetched differently from an If's; it is not -- `br.body` either way -- and the actual distinction is made on the NEXT line, where `subs` walks a single node for an IfExp and iterates the statement list for an If. `body` is then used only in the IfExp arm, so the ternary is dead as well as misleading. No behaviour depends on it and no check catches it; it is the sort of line that makes a later reader believe a distinction was considered where none was. The repair is one line and is in `unfinished`.
